close_reason: Replaced 8 unwrap_or_else(|e| json!(serverFail)) sites with .expect('derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible'). Sites: helpers.rs:13 (set_error_value), calendar.rs:144,190; event.rs:285,389,621; participant_identity.rs:127,169. Workspace tests pass (96 result entries, all ok), clippy clean, fmt clean. Commit c5693e5.
description:
src/helpers.rs:7-11:

    pub(crate) fn set_error_value(e: &crate::backend::SetError) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::to_value(e).unwrap_or_else(
            |err| serde_json::json!({ "type": "serverFail", "description": err.to_string() }),
        )
    }

This silently downgrades a SetError serialization failure to a free-form serverFail with the serde error in the description.  serde_json::to_value cannot fail on a SetError unless the type's Serialize impl panics or hits an integer-overflow edge case — for a stable typed SetError it is effectively infallible. The unwrap_or_else branch is dead code paying for itself in noise.

Two reasonable fixes:
1. Use serde_json::to_value(e).expect("SetError serializes infallibly") with a clear panic message — explicit about the invariant.
2. Use Value::Object("type" -> SetErrorType -> str) directly, bypassing serde for the trivial case.

Either way is more honest than the current silent-fallback. The current form would also obscure a real bug (custom SetErrorType variant with a non-trivial Display impl that fails) by emitting the error as a 'description' field that no client will know to look at.

Aside: the same set_error_value style with .unwrap_or_else appears at 5+ sites in event.rs/calendar.rs/etc. for serde_json::to_value(&created_obj). Same observation applies — Calendar/CalendarEvent/ParticipantIdentity Serialize impls are auto-derived via #[derive(Serialize)] and cannot fail at runtime.

Idiom note: 'unwrap_or_else with an error fallback that hides the real bug' is a known Rust antipattern. .expect() with a clear invariant message is preferable for infallible-in-practice cases.
title: set_error_value swallows serde failure into 'serverFail' description string
